answer: Referral shares fade per recruit on a two-day half-life and are capped at the recruiter's own lifetime earnings, so a dense tree of willow-kin offshoots pays almost nothing. The cost of a sybil tree is therefore the full cost of earning itself, with no oasis leverage from propagation. The engine computes the decay and cap by summing on-chain referral records from the ledge-tagged joins at settlement.
